entities.name: Hendursaga
entities.primary_domains: night watch; heralds; law and order; protection of streets
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Hendursaĝa'; Wiggermann, 'The Gods Išum and Ḫendursanga' (JANER 2010)
entities.note: Divine night-watchman and 'chief herald,' attested in the Lagash pantheon from the Early Dynastic period and later equated with Akkadian Ishum.

entities.name: Ninegal
entities.primary_domains: palaces; royal dynasty; protection of kingship
entities.source: Behrens & Klein, RlA s.v. 'Nin-egal'; Beaulieu studies of Belet-ekallim
entities.note: 'Lady of the Palace' (Akk. Belet-ekallim); oldest attestation is the Early Dynastic Fara god list, later guardian of the royal dynasty across Mesopotamia, Mari and the Hittite world.

entities.name: Nin-MAR.KI
entities.primary_domains: cattle; oaths; long-distance trade; coastal Lagash
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: Divine protector of cattle and oath-deity in the Lagash pantheon, daughter of Nanshe and Nindara, with chief cult center at the sea-port Guabba; attested in Early Dynastic Lagash.

entities.name: Lisin
entities.source: Krebernik & Lisman, 'The Sumerian Zame Hymns from Tell Abū Ṣalābīḫ' (2020); Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Lisin'
entities.note: Originally a goddess addressed as 'mother,' the final deity praised in the Early Dynastic Zame Hymns as tutelary of Abu Salabikh; daughter of Shulpae and Ninhursag.

entities.name: Ninsikila
entities.source: Krebernik & Lisman, Zame Hymns (2020); Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: Spouse of Lisin, male in Early Dynastic sources (Zame Hymns) before a later gender reversal; distinct from the homophonous Dilmunite goddess Meskilak.

entities.name: Ashgi
entities.primary_domains: war; tutelary of Adab and Kesh
entities.source: Such-Gutiérrez, Adab studies; Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Ašgi'
entities.note: Warrior god and original tutelary of Adab, son of Ninhursag and Shulpae, already named in Early Dynastic sources from Fara and the Kesh Temple Hymn.

entities.name: Panigingarra
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Pa(p)-nigin-ĝara'; Such-Gutiérrez, Adab studies
entities.note: Son of Ninhursag and Shulpae worshiped at Adab and associated with his brother Ashgi; attested from the Early Dynastic period and later equated with Ninurta.

entities.name: Pabilsag
entities.source: Wiggermann, RlA s.v. 'Pabilsaĝ'; ORACC AMGG 'Pabilsag'
entities.note: Warrior god first attested in the Early Dynastic IIIa god lists from Fara and Abu Salabikh; husband of the healing goddess Ninisina and father of Damu and Gunura.

entities.name: Ninisina
entities.source: ORACC AMGG 'Ninisinna'; Böck, 'The Healing Goddess Gula' (2014)
entities.note: 'Lady of Isin,' great divine physician first attested in the Fara god lists of the Early Dynastic IIIa period; wife of Pabilsag, later syncretized with Gula.

entities.name: Gunura
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Gunura'; ORACC AMGG 'Ninisinna'
entities.note: Daughter of Ninisina and Pabilsag and sister of the dying healer-god Damu, attested as part of the Isin healing-goddess circle.

entities.name: Gatumdug
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Edzard, RlA s.v. 'Gatumdug'
entities.note: Tutelary goddess of Lagash described metaphorically as its mother in Early Dynastic sources, later honored by Gudea who called her his mother and father.

entities.name: Dumuzi-abzu
entities.primary_domains: fertility; freshwater abzu; tutelary of Kinunir
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: Tutelary goddess of Kinunir near Lagash (also called Kinirša), a female counterpart to Dumuzi attested in the Early Dynastic Lagash state pantheon.

entities.name: Nindara
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nindara'
entities.note: Local Lagash god and husband of Nanshe, attested in the Early Dynastic Lagash pantheon; Selz regards him as elder brother of Hendursaga.

entities.name: Igalima
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Edzard, RlA s.v. 'Igalim(a)'
entities.note: Son of Ningirsu and Bau, the divine 'door of the throne-room'/E-ninnu, receiving offerings already in Early Dynastic Lagash and named on the Gudea cylinders.

entities.name: Shulshaga
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Šul-šaga'
entities.note: Eldest son of Ningirsu and Bau and elder brother of Igalima, attested receiving offerings in Early Dynastic Lagash documents.

entities.name: Shul-utula
entities.source: Selz, FAOS 1995 (Lagaš pantheon); Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: 'Youngling shepherd,' personal god of the Ur-Nanshe dynasty of Lagash, named in Early Dynastic royal inscriptions of Eannatum and Entemena.

entities.name: Lugal-Marada
entities.primary_domains: earth; the plow; tutelary of Marad; war
entities.source: Lambert, RlA s.v. 'Lugal-Marda'; Sjöberg, Temple Hymns
entities.note: City god of Marad, sometimes a manifestation of Ninurta; subject of one of the Temple Hymns, with cult attested from the 3rd millennium.

entities.name: Gibil
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Girra/Gibil'; ORACC AMGG 'Girra'
entities.note: Fire god (Akk. Girra), patron of metalworkers and purification, with earliest attestations in Early Dynastic III administrative texts from Fara and Telloh.

entities.name: Ninildu
entities.source: Krebernik & Lisman, Zame Hymns (2020); Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-ildu'
entities.note: Divine carpenter worshiped at Zabalam, attested in the god lists from Abu Salabikh and Fara and in the Early Dynastic Zame Hymns.

entities.name: Ninmug
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-mug'
entities.note: Divine metalworker/sculptor ('tibira kalamma') and birth-helper of Ninmah, attested in the Early Dynastic Fara god list with cult at Kisiga and Adab.

entities.name: Ninimma
entities.source: Focke, RlA s.v. 'Nin-imma'
entities.note: Divine scholar/scribe and courtier of Enlil who also assisted at birth; attested among the early Nippur circle and in Enki and Ninmah.

entities.name: Ninkurra
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-kurra'; ETCSL 'Enki and Ninhursaĝ'
entities.note: Divine artisan/sculptor of the Enki–Ninhursag generative sequence, mother of Uttu in the Dilmun myth tradition.

entities.name: Ninshar
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-šar'; ETCSL 'Enki and Ninmah'
entities.note: Goddess of the Enki–Ninhursag and Enki–Ninmah birth-helper circle; the theophoric name Ur-Ninšar is common in Early Dynastic and Ur III sources.

entities.name: Ninnigara
entities.source: Krebernik & Lisman, Zame Hymns (2020); Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: Goddess of the niĝar (a birth/temple precinct) linked to birth and healing, attested in the Fara god list and the Early Dynastic Zame Hymns.

entities.name: Ningirima
entities.primary_domains: incantations; ritual purification; snakes; sacred water
entities.source: Krebernik, 'Die Beschwörungen aus Fara und Ebla'; Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-girima'
entities.note: Major Early Dynastic incantation goddess and divine purifier associated with snakes and sacred-water basins, central to the earliest Sumerian magical tradition.

entities.name: Mes-sanga-Unug
entities.source: Krebernik & Lisman, Zame Hymns (2020); Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: Warrior god of Uruk's Kullaba district, 'great ensi of Inanna,' belonging to the earliest Uruk pantheon and named in the Early Dynastic Zame Hymns.

entities.name: Ninirigal
entities.source: Krebernik & Lisman, Zame Hymns (2020); Cavigneaux & Krebernik, RlA
entities.note: Tutelary goddess of Uruk's Kullaba district, counted among the chief deities praised in the opening Early Dynastic hymns.

entities.name: Nirah
entities.source: Wiggermann, RlA s.v. 'Niraḫ, Irḫan'; ORACC AMGG 'Ištaran'
entities.note: Serpent god and messenger of Ishtaran of Der, depicted as a snake; worship attested from the late Early Dynastic period.

entities.name: Ningirida
entities.primary_domains: underworld (by association); chthonic family of Ninazu
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-girida'; Wiggermann studies of Ninazu
entities.note: Wife of the chthonic god Ninazu and mother of Ningishzida, appearing alongside Ninazu from the Ur III period.

entities.name: Ninura
entities.primary_domains: tutelary of Umma; consort cult of Shara
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-ura'; Selz, Umma studies
entities.note: Goddess of the Umma region and wife of Shara, attested only in third-millennium sources before being displaced by Inanna of Zabalam.

entities.name: Ninti
entities.primary_domains: the rib / life ('lady of life'); healing
entities.source: Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nin-ti'; ETCSL 'Enki and Ninhursaĝ'
entities.note: 'Lady of the rib/life,' one of the eight healing deities born of Ninhursag in the Dilmun myth; attested near Ninkasi in a Fara-period document.

entities.name: Nungal
entities.source: Civil, 'On Mesopotamian Jails and their Lady Warden'; Krebernik, RlA s.v. 'Nungal'
entities.note: Goddess of prisons and divine sifter of the guilty from the innocent, a daughter-in-law of Enlil whose name is attested already in the Early Dynastic period.

relationships.rationale: Hendursaga is equated with Akkadian Ishum in god lists from the Old Babylonian period onward.
Hendursaga belongs to the Lagash state pantheon centered on Nanshe's circle.
He is the divine night-watchman and herald who guards streets at night.
'Lady of the Palace' served as protectress of the royal dynasty and palace.
Ninegal/Belet-ekallim was at times drawn into the orbit of Ishtar in palace cult.
Nin-MAR.KI is the daughter of Nanshe and Nindara in the Lagash pantheon.
Her father is Nindara, husband of Nanshe.
She was the divine protector of cattle.
Lisin is daughter of Ninhursag and Shulpae.
Ninsikila is the spouse of Lisin in Early Dynastic sources.
Ninsikila is consort of Lisin in the Zame Hymns tradition.
Ashgi is son of Ninhursag and Shulpae.
Ashgi and Panigingarra are both sons of Ninhursag at Adab.
The Kesh Temple Hymn characterizes Ashgi as a warrior god.
Panigingarra is son of Ninhursag and Shulpae per An=Anum and the Weidner list.
In late sources he could be equated with Ninurta.
Pabilsag is the husband of Ninisina.
Pabilsag was at times equated with Ninurta as a warrior god.
Pabilsag is fundamentally a warrior god in the early tradition.
Ninisina is wife of Pabilsag.
Ninisina is mother of the healer-god Damu.
Ninisina is the great divine physician of Isin.
Ninisina was syncretized with the healing goddess Gula.
Gunura is daughter of Ninisina and Pabilsag.
Gunura is sister of Damu and mourns his death in laments.
Gatumdug was metaphorically the mother of Lagash and of its rulers.
Gatumdug belongs to the Lagash state pantheon headed by Ningirsu.
Dumuzi-abzu is part of the Lagash state pantheon associated with Nanshe.
Her name links her to the freshwater abzu.
Nindara is the husband of Nanshe.
Nindara and Nanshe are parents of Nin-MAR.KI.
Igalima is son of Ningirsu and Bau.
Bau is Igalima's mother.
Igalima is the younger brother of Shulshaga.
Shulshaga is the eldest son of Ningirsu and Bau.
Bau is Shulshaga's mother.
Shul-utula functions within the Lagash pantheon as personal god of its Ningirsu-devoted dynasty.
As a personal/family god he interceded for and protected his charges.
Lugal-Marada was regarded as a manifestation of Ninurta.
He was associated with the earth and the plow.
Gibil/Girra is the fire god.
He is patron of metallurgists and called founder of cities.
Fire/purification deities were associated with Enki/Ea's sphere of incantation and ritual.
Ninildu is the divine carpenter.
Divine craftsmen belong to Enki/Ea's circle of artisan deities.
Ninmug is the divine metalworker and sculptor 'of the land'.
She doubles as a birth-goddess and assistant of Ninmah.
Ninimma is a courtier of Enlil at Nippur.
She is a divine scribe/scholar and birth-helper.
In the Enki and Ninhursag myth Ninkurra is a daughter of Enki.
Ninkurra is a divine sculptor/stone-worker.
Ninshar is one of the birth-helper assistants of Ninmah/Ninhursag in Enki and Ninmah.
She assists with birth in the creation-of-mankind myth.
Ninnigara is associated with birth via the niĝar precinct.
The niĝar she personifies is a part of temples of Ninisina and Inanna.
Ningirima is the divine purifier and exorcist of the earliest incantation tradition.
She became associated with basins of sacred water.
She shares the incantation/purification sphere later dominated by Enki/Ea and his son Asalluhi.
He is described as the 'great ensi of Inanna' in the earliest Uruk sources.
He was regarded as a warrior deity of Uruk's Kullaba.
Ninirigal is tutelary of Kullaba, the Uruk district of Inanna, listed among the chief Zame deities.
She functions as tutelary protector of the Kullaba district.
Nirah is the divine messenger of Ishtaran of Der.
Ishtaran could be regarded as Nirah's father.
Ningirida is the wife of Ninazu.
Ningirida is mother of Ningishzida.
She belongs to the chthonic family of Ninazu and Ningishzida.
Ninura is the wife of Shara of Umma.
She functioned as a tutelary goddess of the Umma region.
Ninti is one of the eight deities born of Ninhursag in the Enki and Ninhursag myth.
'Lady of life/the rib' belongs to the healing-by-birth tradition.
Nungal is a courtier and daughter-in-law of Enlil.
She judges and separates the guilty from the innocent as goddess of prisons.
She is sometimes associated with the underworld.
